title: Articles: un, une, des, le, la, les
goal: Choose between un, une, des and le, la, l', les, and understand why French nouns almost always need an article.

drills.en: I have an aunt in Moncton.

drills.explain: Plural, not yet identified → des. English often says nothing here; French needs des.
A specific person: le mari de Sofia = Sofia's husband.

drills.text: ___ oncle de Mei habite à Québec.
drills.en: Mei's uncle lives in Québec City.
drills.explain: oncle starts with a vowel → l'.

drills.prompt: How do you say “Children are funny” (children in general)?
drills.explain: General statements use le / la / les in French.

items.note: The h is silent, so: l'homme, un‿homme, les‿hommes.

example.fr: Ils ont un garçon et une fille.
example.en: They have a boy and a girl.

items.note: Always une personne, even for a man.

example.en: Lucie's baby is six months old.

items.note: Always un bébé, even for a baby girl.

blocks.title: After a newcomers' picnic in Ottawa
blocks.context: Nguyen and Camille look at a group photo.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Qui est la femme blonde, ici ?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: C'est Sofia. C'est une amie. Elle est mexicaine.
lines.en: That's Sofia. She's a friend. She's Mexican.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: C'est le mari de Sofia, Alex. Il est très drôle.
lines.en: That's Sofia's husband, Alex. He's very funny.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Ce sont les enfants de Sofia et d'Alex : un garçon et une fille.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Oui ! Les enfants sont drôles, et les parents sont très gentils.

blocks.body: Count the articles: [[la femme]], [[une amie]], [[l'homme]], [[le mari]], [[les enfants]], [[un garçon]], [[une fille]]. In French, almost every noun comes with one. [[Ce sont]] is simply the plural of [[c'est]]: *they are / these are*.

blocks.title: Articles
head: masculine
feminine
plural
blocks.note: [[L']] replaces [[le]] or [[la]] before a vowel or a silent h: [[l'enfant]], [[l'amie]], [[l'homme]]. The plural forms [[des]] and [[les]] are the same for both genders.

blocks.title: un, une, des: one of many, not identified yet
blocks.body:
Use [[un]] / [[une]] / [[des]] for a person or thing you mention for the first time, or one among many:

- [[J'ai un frère et une sœur.]] = I have a brother and a sister.
- [[C'est une amie.]] = She's a friend (one of my friends).
- [[Raj a des cousins à Vancouver.]] = Raj has (some) cousins in Vancouver.

[[Des]] is the plural of un / une. English often uses **nothing** there; French can't.

blocks.title: le, la, les: this specific one, or in general
blocks.body:
Use [[le]] / [[la]] / [[l']] / [[les]] when you mean a **specific, known** person or thing:

- [[C'est le mari de Sofia.]] = That's Sofia's husband (she has only one!).
- [[Et les enfants ?]] = And the children (in the photo)?

French **also** uses le / la / les for **general statements**, where English uses no article at all:

- [[Les enfants sont drôles.]] = Children are funny (children in general).

blocks.title: “X's Y” in French
blocks.pattern: le / la / les + person or thing + de + owner
blocks.note: French has no *'s*. Say “the brother of Mei”. Before a vowel, [[de]] becomes [[d']].

blocks.title: Why French needs articles
blocks.body:
A French noun almost never stands alone. One big reason: you often **can't hear** if a noun is singular or plural. [[frère]] and [[frères]] sound exactly the same. The article does that job: [[le frère]] / [[les frères]], [[un enfant]] / [[des enfants]].

The article also tells you the **gender**, which then changes adjectives and possessives. That is why it's best to learn every noun with [[un]] or [[une]]: [[un oncle]], [[une tante]].

You already know some places with **no** article: after [[être]] with a nationality ([[Je suis canadien.]]), and after [[mon / ma / mes]] etc., which **replace** the article ([[mon frère]], never *le mon frère*).

blocks.title: Grammar gender is not biology
blocks.body:
Gender in French is a grammar label. For people, it usually matches: [[un oncle]], [[une tante]]. But a few words keep one gender for everyone:

- [[une personne]] is always feminine: [[Karim est une personne gentille.]]
- [[un bébé]] is always masculine, even a baby girl.

The adjective agrees with the word, not the real person: [[une personne sérieuse]].

examples.fr: Alex est une personne très drôle.
examples.en: Alex is a very funny person.

examples.fr: Le bébé de Mei est petit.

blocks.body:
- [[le]] sounds like *luh*; [[les]] rhymes with *é*. This tiny difference is often the **only** clue to singular or plural: [[le cousin]] / [[les cousins]].
- [[un]] is a nasal vowel; [[une]] ends with a clear *n*: [[une tante]].
- Liaison before a vowel: [[un‿ami]], [[des‿enfants]], [[les‿hommes]] (z sound).

- **No article:** [[J'ai frères]] → [[J'ai des frères]]. [[Enfants sont drôles]] → [[Les enfants sont drôles]].
- **le / la before a vowel:** [[le enfant]], [[la amie]] → [[l'enfant]], [[l'amie]].
- **Article with a nationality:** [[Je suis une canadienne]] → [[Je suis canadienne]].
- **Article plus possessive:** [[le mon frère]] → [[mon frère]].

blocks.title: Preview: articles after a negative
blocks.body:
Just to recognise for now. After a negative, [[un]], [[une]] and [[des]] usually become [[de]] (or [[d']] before a vowel):

- [[J'ai un frère.]] → [[Je n'ai pas de frère.]]
- [[J'ai des enfants.]] → [[Je n'ai pas d'enfants.]]

You will learn negative sentences properly in a later unit.

blocks.title: One word, three meanings
blocks.body: Articles and context matter. [[Une blonde]] can be *a blond woman* anywhere. In Québec, [[ma blonde]] means *my girlfriend*. And in a bar, [[une blonde]] can also be a light beer (a lager)!

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: C'est ma famille, sur la photo. C'est mon oncle, Ahmed, et c'est la femme d'Ahmed, Leila. Ils ont un garçon et une fille. Les enfants sont très drôles !
models.en: This is my family, in the photo. That's my uncle, Ahmed, and that's Ahmed's wife, Leila. They have a boy and a girl. The children are very funny!

blocks.prompt: Write about four people in your wider family or circle of friends: aunts, uncles, cousins, friends. Say where they live or what they are like.
checklist: Use un / une / des at least twice
Use le / la / l' / les at least twice
Use X de Y (the husband of…) once
Learn the gender: une personne, un bébé

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: J'ai un oncle et une tante à Moncton. J'ai aussi des cousins à Montréal. La fille de mon oncle a un bébé. Le bébé a trois mois. Mon amie Mei est une personne très gentille.
models.en: I have an uncle and an aunt in Moncton. I also have cousins in Montréal. My uncle's daughter has a baby. The baby is three months old. My friend Mei is a very kind person.

summary:
- Use [[un / une / des]] for someone mentioned for the first time, and [[le / la / l' / les]] for someone specific or for things in general
- Use [[l']] before a vowel or silent h: [[l'enfant, l'homme, l'amie]]
- Say *X's Y* as [[le frère de Mei]]
- Remember that French needs an article where English often has none: [[J'ai des cousins. Les enfants sont drôles.]]
